description:
SCD2 audit finding #5 (two latent, non-shipping observations).
(1) The validation id one_current_per_business_key (HAVING COUNT(*) <> 1 over
is_current rows) catches duplicate current versions but not zero-current keys,
so it enforces "at most one", not "exactly one" as the name implied. Each op
already backstops the existence side with a positive companion check, so the
exactly-one guarantee holds collectively. (2) The row_hash '|'-delimited /
CAST(... AS VARCHAR) fingerprint is TPC-H-safe (0 pipe chars at SF0.01,
same-engine comparison) but not injection-safe over arbitrary data.
Decision (w0): rename the invariant honestly (no hot-path SQL change, so the
benchmark timings the blog cites are unaffected) and document the fingerprint's
safety assumptions in code.

work_units.summary: Re-ran the zero-current probe: at_most check caught 0 offending, companion every_changed_key_has_current_staged_version caught 20 -> backstop confirmed, hardening-only.
Renamed one_current_per_business_key -> at_most_one_current_per_business_key across all 3 SCD2 ops in operations.yaml and the registration assertion in test_write_primitives_core.py:625.
Documented _scd2_row_hash_expr safety in code: same-engine comparison only, and '|' delimiter collision-safety scoped to TPC-H (0 pipe chars); flags reuse over arbitrary data.
Ran SCD2 unit + DuckDB integration tests (16 -k scd2 + 59 core unit, all green); ruff check/format clean on touched files.
